title: Main menu ignores the persisted text-size setting
evidence: With Settings.text_scale=2.0 before instantiating menu.tscn, the real menu still reports New Game/Continue/Quit font16, subtitle14 and version11. menu.gd applies fixed overrides and never reads text_scale. Captured in panels_project/controls_probe_results.json menu.
reproduction: Set Text Size to200% in a game, return to Main Menu or restart with that setting persisted.
impact: Navigation returns to small text precisely for players who selected enlarged text.
recommendation: Apply the persisted text scale to startup controls and adapt the centered menu layout to the resulting dimensions.
acceptance: Startup and return-to-menu controls honor100/125/150/175/200% consistently; every action remains visible and operable.

title: Accessibility settings cannot be opened before starting a game
evidence: The startup menu offers only New Game, Continue and Quit. Settings is constructed in ui.gd after the main scene opens, so a first-time user cannot choose reduced motion or enlarged text from the entry screen.
reproduction: Start without a saved preference file and look for accessibility controls before choosing New Game.
impact: Players must navigate and view the game with default presentation before they can configure it.
recommendation: Expose the shared Settings panel from the startup menu, applying options immediately to the startup scene as appropriate.
acceptance: A first launch allows changing motion, contrast, palette, packet style and text size without creating or loading a run.

title: Continue provides no description of the saved run
evidence: Continue is a single static button whose enabled state comes from Session.has_save(); no timestamp, seed, progress or saved-run summary is presented. Save validation/backup bugs are owned by the simulation audit, not this item.
reproduction: Return after several sessions and inspect Continue before loading.
impact: Players cannot confirm which run they will resume or whether it is the expected save.
recommendation: Show a concise save preview with save time and meaningful run progress, plus an explanatory empty state when no save exists.
acceptance: Before continuing, the saved run can be identified from its timestamp/progress; preview failure never blocks valid backup recovery.

title: Startup menu has no initial keyboard focus
evidence: menu._ready creates buttons but never selects a focus target. The real-scene probe records initial_focus.path='null'. Keyboard Tab can initiate navigation; this proposal improves immediate discoverability rather than claiming keyboard navigation is impossible.
reproduction: Launch using a keyboard and look for a focused default action before pressing Tab.
impact: There is no visible starting point or immediately actionable default for keyboard users.
recommendation: Focus Continue when a usable save is available, otherwise New Game, and retain a clear focus indicator.
acceptance: The entry menu has one sensible initial focus target; Enter/Space activates it and all actions remain reachable with Tab/Shift+Tab.

title: Keyboard focus escapes blocking modals and activates background controls
evidence: _grab_modal_focus assigns only the initial button. Actual Tab events in controls_probe move Settings Off→Off→Off→Code→100%→Close→Build→Tech→Stats. Enter press/release then changes ui.tab tostats while settings_visible remains true. No focus containment or background-control guard exists.
reproduction: Open Settings, press Tab six times, then activate a background tab; repeat focus traversal around pause/win boundaries.
impact: A blocking modal permits hidden/background UI actions, undermining input isolation and potentially exposing Load/Quit controls through keyboard traversal.
recommendation: Trap forward/backward focus within the topmost modal and prevent background UI actions while it is open.
acceptance: Tab/Shift+Tab wrap within Settings, Pause and Victory, including nested Settings; Enter/Space never activates controls behind the modal.

title: Closing a nested modal loses keyboard focus instead of restoring its opener
evidence: _close_settings hides the overlay and restores paused state only. When Settings is opened over Pause then closed, controls_probe records nested_settings_closed_focus.path='null'; the Pause overlay remains open without restoring its Settings button or another meaningful focus target.
reproduction: Open Pause, keyboard-activate Settings, then Close/Esc the Settings panel.
impact: Keyboard users lose their location after returning to the parent menu.
recommendation: Track the opening control or a modal focus stack and restore a valid visible target when each modal closes.
acceptance: Close and Esc return focus to the corresponding visible opener for nested Settings, Menu-tab Settings and Victory dismissal; invalid openers fall back predictably.

title: Enlarged victory results push both exit actions below the viewport
evidence: At200% and1280×720 the actual victory panel extends to y891; Main Menu starts y822 and ends y883. At1024×600 the configured stretch gives logical1280×750 but the panel still ends906;1366×768 gives the same1280×720 logical overflow. Settings and Pause fit in these checks, so this is one victory-content overflow finding. Results are in controls_probe_results.json modal_sizes.
reproduction: Reach the Cash goal with Text Size200%, including a scorecard with multi-digit statistics.
impact: Keep Playing and Main Menu are outside the visible viewport; the modal offers no scrolling path to those controls.
recommendation: Constrain the victory panel to the viewport, place results in an internal scroll area and retain visible action controls; center based on final size.
acceptance: At all supported text scales and tested aspect ratios, the entire action area is visible and focusable; long scorecards can be read without pushing actions offscreen.

title: Primary navigation tab names are truncated at large text sizes
evidence: Five tabs share284px regardless of font scale. At200% screenshots14_menu_200.png and17_jobs_200.png show Bu/Te/St/Jo/Me rather than full names; clip_text is enabled globally and no tooltip or accessible full-label fallback is assigned. This differs from palette-child overlap in UI-PANELS-01.
reproduction: Set Text Size200%, close Settings and read the five primary sidebar tabs.
impact: The navigation destinations become ambiguous abbreviations generated by clipping.
recommendation: Use a responsive tab arrangement, wrap/stack labels or combine stable icons with full accessible names and visible destination help.
acceptance: Each destination is identifiable at every text scale without guessing clipped text; focus and selected-tab feedback stay clear.

title: Exit and Load actions replace unsaved progress without a save decision
evidence: Menu buttons call go_main_menu, quit_game and load_game directly; go_main_menu/quit_game switch/exit immediately and no autosave or dirty-run decision is implemented. This proposal concerns the user flow, separate from save format/validation defects.
reproduction: Change the network after the last manual save, then choose Main Menu, Quit or Load Game from the Menu/Pause UI.
impact: A single menu action can discard the player's latest network changes without revealing that outcome.
recommendation: Track unsaved progress and offer Save/Discard/Cancel before destructive session replacement; keep the flow concise when the run is already saved.
acceptance: A dirty run can be saved or retained before exit/load; Cancel restores the same run and focus, while an already-saved run exits without redundant prompts.

title: Load Game remains available when there is no save to load
evidence: Startup Continue is disabled based on Session.has_save, but Menu/Pause Load Game is always an active button connected directly to main.load_game. No corresponding availability state or reason is supplied.
reproduction: Start a fresh isolated game with no primary/backup save and open Menu or Pause.
impact: The menu presents an unavailable operation and defers the explanation until the player invokes it.
recommendation: Reflect save availability consistently in Load Game controls and explain the unavailable state, refreshing after Save or external save changes.
acceptance: Without a primary or valid backup, Load is visibly unavailable with a readable reason; saving enables it, and usable backup recovery remains available.

title: Settings options lack descriptions of their visible effects
evidence: Settings contains only option labels and short values such as On/Off or Code/Dots. There are no explanatory tooltips, descriptions or previews for what motion is reduced, what contrast changes, or what packet Code/Dots means.
reproduction: Open Settings and compare Packet style, Reduced motion and High contrast before changing them.
impact: Players must experiment to learn whether an option addresses their readability or motion needs.
recommendation: Add concise descriptions or previews of each option's user-visible scope, including that motion reduction preserves the information needed to follow traffic.
acceptance: Every option's effect can be understood before activation; descriptions remain accessible at200% and through keyboard focus.

title: Text size is a hidden cyclic sequence rather than a directly selectable value
evidence: _toggle_setting('ts') advances100→125→150→175→200→100. The control shows only the current value, so reaching a smaller adjacent size can require cycling through every larger value and an abrupt reset.
reproduction: Choose150%, then try reducing to125% or previewing several values.
impact: Adjusting readability is slower and the wraparound is undisclosed.
recommendation: Use a labelled choice list or bounded decrease/increase controls with an explicit default/reset action.
acceptance: Any supported value can be selected directly or with predictable bounded steps; increasing at200% never silently jumps to100%.

title: Inspector actions sit after long flavour text and technical details
evidence: info_body precedes every action and begins with d.homage; critical Status is appended near its end. In the200% probe the body ends y1335, first action starts1341 and rate controls start1542 inside a scroll viewport ending667. Actions remain scrollable, but require traversing the entire prose block. This is separate from the global status-line height finding.
reproduction: Select a producer at200% text and attempt to quickly disable it or reduce output during a network problem.
impact: Time-sensitive controls and operational status are far below descriptive prose.
recommendation: Put state and main operational controls near the top or in a bounded persistent action area; move flavour/extended metrics into a secondary section.
acceptance: Disable/output actions and current status are quickly reachable from the initial inspector position at all scales; full descriptive details remain available.

title: Overclock lacks cost, duration and remaining-boost context
evidence: The action label is only ⚡ Overclock(O), with empty tooltip. main.gd defines20 Cycles/20 seconds and sets boost_t, but inspector shows no remaining duration or active boost label; probe boost_time20 is visible only as a doubled Produces value. Functional disabled/offline overclock guards are owned by the simulation audit.
reproduction: Select a producer, inspect Overclock before using it, then return to that producer during its20-second boost.
impact: Players spend a resource without a preview and cannot tell when the temporary effect will end or whether another press is useful.
recommendation: Display the cost and effect duration before activation, then show boost state/countdown and current affordability.
acceptance: The control explains20 Cycles→2× output for20s and shows remaining boost time; a resource shortage has an explicit reason.

title: Output adjustment buttons remain enabled at their limits
evidence: Main clamps cap_rate to0..1, but _update_info never updates rate_down/rate_up disabled states. Probe reports minus enabled at0% and plus enabled at100%, so these presses generate messages without changing output.
reproduction: Select a producer at100% and press+, or reduce it to0% and press−.
impact: The control offers an action that has no effect and obscures the supported output range.
recommendation: Disable the appropriate endpoint button and identify the range/step size in its help; provide explicit accessible names for increase/decrease.
acceptance: Minus is unavailable at0%, plus at100%, and adjustments between boundaries clearly move by25 percentage points.

title: Inspector does not distinguish potential capacity from actual current throughput
evidence: Producer lines use _production, so disabling a producer removes its potential output/coverage information entirely; processors always display nominal CONV.rate 'atN/s while linked' without current input/fuel/route bottlenecks. Neither presentation reports delivered-to-C2 throughput or a clear rated-versus-current distinction.
reproduction: Inspect a disabled producer or a connected processor with no Intel/fuel, then compare the displayed rate with actual traffic.
impact: Players cannot judge what a disabled node could recover or why an apparently rated processor is idle.
recommendation: Separate rated capacity, current production/processing, delivered throughput and a concise idle/limited reason; retain capacity information while disabled.
acceptance: An idle processor identifies the limiting input/fuel/route; a disabled producer retains rated capacity while current output is0; delivery loss is not presented as raw production.

title: Tunnel latency uses packet units for a route-length count
evidence: The inspector labels _edge_len as Latency:N pkt, but main.gd:735–737 returns path.size(), a cell count. Packet motion depends on PACKET_SPEED/slow_factor, so this count does not directly communicate elapsed delivery time.
reproduction: Inspect a short and long tunnel and try to infer when a packet will reach the parent from the displayed latency.
impact: The central timing metric has an unclear unit and cannot be readily related to travel time.
recommendation: Label route length in cells/tiles and provide an estimated travel time in seconds using the actual path/speed, with variable slowdown qualified.
acceptance: Every displayed metric has a coherent unit; players can compare route length and approximate link travel time without interpreting 'packet latency'.

title: Tunnel overload advice has no contextual upgrade or reroute action
evidence: The overload text recommends a fatter tunnel or alternate route, but the selected-tunnel branch exposes only remove_btn. Improving the link requires dismantling it, re-opening Build→Links, reselecting endpoints and rebuilding.
reproduction: Select an overloaded DNS tunnel and follow the inspector's recommendation to use a higher-capacity tunnel.
impact: Diagnosing a bottleneck is separated from the corrective action by several navigation and placement steps.
recommendation: Offer an Upgrade/Reroute flow from the selected link with protocol metrics, cost and route preview, committing atomically with undo support.
acceptance: A selected bottleneck can be upgraded/rerouted from its inspector; a failed or cancelled preview preserves the existing connection and resources.

title: Dismantle does not preview the affected branch or refund outcome
evidence: The button is labelled Dismantle(Del) with no impact tooltip. main._remove_node removes the selected node and detaches incoming children; dismantling does not call _refund, while Ctrl+Z restores the removed topology.
reproduction: Select a relay/processor with incoming branches and inspect Dismantle before activating it.
impact: Players cannot see how many structures lose their C2 route or whether build resources return before the action.
recommendation: Show affected direct/descendant nodes, resource outcome and undo availability near Dismantle; distinguish removing a node from removing its outbound tunnel.
acceptance: Before removal the inspector explains the resulting disconnected branch and refund policy; the subsequent undo restores the described topology.

title: Same-type tunnel endpoints have indistinguishable inspector names
evidence: main._node_name returns the type name and the tunnel inspector concatenates those names. With two legal same-type node fixtures, controls_probe records 'Links Mirai Dropper → Mirai Dropper'. No instance ID, location or jump action identifies source versus parent.
reproduction: Connect one Mirai Dropper to another and select that tunnel.
impact: The inspector cannot identify which actual structures the selected link connects, especially in a large network.
recommendation: Include stable instance IDs/names or coordinates for both endpoints and allow selecting/jumping to each endpoint.
acceptance: Any two same-type endpoints have distinct readable identities; the displayed direction can be matched to the actual source and parent.
